team_results.recap: Detroit led 21-0 before New Orleans — as the flagged depleted secondary and 49.5 total both foreshadowed — stormed back to tie it 24-24 late in regulation, forcing overtime. Jahmyr Gibbs (3 TD, 156 yards) and a Goff-to-St. Brown OT score pulled out a 31-30 win after New Orleans' 2-point try for the outright win failed. The Skeptic's secondary-depletion flag was directionally right even though DET escaped with the pick intact.

Dallas lost 28-20 at the Giants despite entering as road favorites; the Skeptic's rebuttal — that the rebuilt post-Parsons-trade defense was a real liability, not added strength — played out as New York piled up 394 total yards to Dallas's 244 and controlled the game with an 8-minute third-quarter drive.

Tennessee was outgained 361-195 and held to a garbage-time touchdown in a 23-10 loss to the Jets, whose defense limited Cam Ward to 140 yards passing and 68 rushing yards allowed. It's the Titans' sixth straight season-opening loss.

The Jets beat Tennessee 23-10, outgaining the Titans 361-195. QB Justin Fields/OC Frank Reich's offense scored on an opening 8-play drive and the defense limited Cam Ward to 140 yards passing behind a strong Aaron Glenn-coached unit in year two.

The Giants beat Dallas 28-20 on Sunday Night Football, John Harbaugh's debut win, behind Jaxson Dart (230 yards passing, 3 TD, 0 INT, plus 54 rushing yards) and a 394-244 total-yardage edge. Dart became the first QB in NFL history to open a season with 3 pass TD, 50+ rush yards, and a 130+ rating — the pregame 'unproven Dart/Skattebo combo' negative didn't hold up at all.

Arizona's stunning 26-14 win — Jacoby Brissett throwing for 277 yards/1 TD, Trey McBride going for 95 yards/1 TD, rookie HC Mike LaFleur winning his debut — was the NFL's biggest Week 1 upset, coming from the week's single lowest win probability on the board (14%).

lessons_learned.lesson: A trap flag backed by a concrete, quantifiable signal (reverse line movement plus a specific personnel weakness — LAC's OL/QB mobility issues) called the week's biggest upset correctly, while a trap flag built mainly on narrative (JAX's 'post-breakout letdown' and 'new DC is unknown' framing, with no concrete weakness identified) was a clean false alarm. Weight trap flags toward cases with at least one hard, checkable signal (line movement, a specific missing/injured starter) over pure storyline/vibes-based reasoning.

The no-lazy-favorite policy passed its first live test: the excluded largest Vegas favorite (LAC, 85% raw implied) suffered the week's biggest upset loss while the recommendation that went to the next-best team (DET) won, saving a pick outright. This is early evidence (n=1 week) that the policy's premise — the single largest raw-ML favorite is exactly where market/public overconfidence is most likely to get punished — has real teeth, not just theoretical justification. Continue applying it without softening.

The archived Week 1 board (data/history/week_analysis_2026_wk01.json) was missing entries for 4 of the week's 32 teams (SEA, NE, LA, SF — the SEA@NE and LA@SF games), even though every other game's both sides were represented. Future survivor-pick runs should verify all 32 teams for the week appear in the board before archiving/overwriting — a missing team can't be graded later and silently shrinks the calibration sample.
